decision: Offers live in a wallet with amounts hidden until you tap the eye, the privacy pattern popularized by digital banks
why: People review offers at work and on shared screens; salary is the most sensitive number in the product.
value: Safe to open anywhere, and screen readers hear 'amount hidden' instead of dots.

decision: The wallet compares net per month in reais, with every deduction as a signed bar: FX spread, company taxes, accountant and bank fees, health insurance, a suggested reserve
why: Brazilians paid in USD compare a gross dollar number with a net reais number and overestimate by a third; the waterfall shows where it goes.
alternative: Show gross salaries side by side.
value: An apples-to-apples decision between a USD contract and a BRL counter-offer.

decision: FX is a static fixture and the scenario slider recomputes net pay locally; the AI note finds the break-even rate by bisection
why: The free-tier rules forbid a rates API, and a scenario is more honest than a live number that changes tomorrow anyway.
value: Zero network calls, and the member sees that the real bet is the exchange rate.

decision: Accept opens a bottom sheet with a biometric-style confirmation; confirming moves the Pipeline card, archives other processes with polite notes and sets a contract reminder, across tabs
why: Accepting is irreversible in real life; a deliberate confirmation and a visible list of consequences prevent mistakes.
value: One confirmation does the tedious follow-up the member would otherwise forget.

decision: The accepted offer is shared like the plan: localStorage plus a BroadcastChannel, read by the board
why: The wallet and the board are different pages and often different tabs; they must agree immediately.
value: Every open Atlas tab reflects the decision at once.
